sections.h2: What sets a fast sale in Beaumont apart
sections.html:
On the Neches River, Beaumont is a port and refinery city whose housing market rises and falls with industry. Sellers commonly face older houses, mixed neighborhoods and a county tax system that works through its own appraisal district.

The mid-2025 estimate is 112,967 residents, 1.8% below the April 2020 base. With shoppers in no rush, the sellers who close soonest are those with a clear tax statement and a clean deed. Many houses go back to the oil booms of the early twentieth century and may predate modern code, which means questions about age and condition are routine.

The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $166,400, and 55.3% of units are lived in by owners. Median gross rent comes to $1,121.

sections.h2: Who collects tax on a Beaumont house, and when it goes late
sections.html:
Your bill involves three separate bodies. The Jefferson Central Appraisal District sets the value, every taxing unit picks its own rate, and the Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector receives the payment. The appraisal district never levies or collects a dollar.

January 1 is the valuation date, and it is also when that year's lien attaches. Bills go out in October. Pay through January 31 and you owe nothing extra; February 1 brings a six percent penalty plus one percent interest from the collector.

  • Get a payoff statement from the tax office before you sign a contract.
  • Find out whether an earlier year's balance is still on the account.
  • Hold on to the receipt for the title company.

sections.h2: Homestead breaks for a seller or buyer
sections.html:
School districts exempt $140,000 for a buyer who moves in, with another $60,000 for school taxes if that buyer is 65 or disabled. Cities and counties can adopt homestead exemptions too.

Tax freezes for older and disabled owners come from the school districts, Jefferson County and the City of Port Arthur. Nothing is charged to file, and if you missed the April 30 date you may still apply within two years after the bill went delinquent.

The 10% annual limit on a homestead's taxable value is a separate cap. For the 2024 through 2026 tax years, other real property worth $5,000,000 or less also has a 20% circuit breaker. New rooms and pools are outside both.

sections.h2: If a Beaumont appraisal looks too high
sections.html:
Your written protest is due on the later of May 15 and the thirtieth day after the notice was mailed. Home notices typically arrive in mid-April, and an appraiser will offer an informal review before the board hears the case.

After an adverse ruling from the Appraisal Review Board, you may file suit in district court within 60 days of getting the written decision. The other choice is binding arbitration, available to every residential homestead whatever its value.

  • Sales of comparable Beaumont houses from around January 1.
  • Photos of foundation, plumbing or roof trouble.
  • A survey, if the district's measurements seem wrong.

sections.h2: Foreclosure timing on a Beaumont home
sections.html:
Because Texas home loans usually include a power of sale, a lender needs no judge to put the house up for auction. Sales take place on a first Tuesday between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., at a site the commissioners court designates.

A default notice starts a 20-day window to pay what you owe and halt the process. After that the lender sends a notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction. A shortfall can still be pursued in court for two years. To sell before the auction, ask the servicer for a payoff letter now.

If the owner left a will, it should be probated within four years of the death, and a muniment of title can carry the house when the sole debts are liens on it. Without a will, a small estate affidavit handles estates of $75,000 or less outside the homestead, though it is no help with other land.

An affidavit of heirship is a sworn paper that no court verifies, and a title insurer may decline it. A transfer on death deed avoids probate entirely when it was recorded before the owner passed. Heirs living in the house can have the homestead exemption continued on the property by giving the appraisal district the death certificate and an ownership affidavit.

sections.h2: Choosing between a listing and a cash sale
sections.html:
An agent makes sense for a house in decent shape when you can sit through showings and wait on a buyer's loan. A cash buyer makes sense when the roof, plumbing or foundation needs work, a tenant lives there, taxes are behind, or a lender or court has set your deadline. The offer is usually lower, but you cover no repairs and you choose the closing date.

Either way, begin with three documents: a tax payoff statement, a mortgage payoff letter and a copy of your deed. Together they show what you will net and reveal any problem before a buyer does.

sections.h2: What happens between contract and closing
sections.html:
A signed contract sends the file to the title company, which reviews the tax account, requests every payoff and searches for liens. You then sign the deed before a notary, and the county clerk records it once funds arrive. Skip the recording and your name stays on the tax roll, since the appraisal district follows recorded deeds.

Schedule your move-out and key handover for the funding date, and file copies of the settlement statement and recorded deed.

Anyone planning nightly stays needs a city permit first. Beaumont asks for one whenever guests stay fewer than 30 consecutive days. Planning and Community Development issues it, and it has to be renewed every year.

Each online listing must show the permit number, and a hotel occupancy tax certificate comes with the package. Advertising before you are permitted can bring a fine, so a buyer with this plan should learn the process before closing.

Deeds for land in the county are kept by the Jefferson County Clerk. To be accepted, a deed must carry a signature and an acknowledgment.

The 2023 clerk manual shows a $5.00 charge for the first page and $4.00 for each extra page, plus records fees of as much as $10 apiece for management and archives. Ownership on the tax roll changes only when the appraisal district sees a recorded deed, so a mismatch there often means a recording was missed.

faqs.q: Does a Beaumont seller pay a state transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. Texas charges recording fees on a deed but no transfer tax, and the Jefferson County Clerk can quote the exact fees.

faqs.q: What date do Beaumont taxes become late?
faqs.a: Most bills turn delinquent on February 1. They are mailed in October with a general payment deadline of January 31.

faqs.q: Is a Beaumont homestead exemption still available if I forgot to file?
faqs.a: Most likely yes. Jefferson Central Appraisal District will take a late homestead application for two years after that year's tax became delinquent.

faqs.q: Do Beaumont short-term rentals need permits?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 30 consecutive days call for a city permit and a hotel occupancy tax certificate, and each listing must display the permit number.

faqs.q: Who hears a protest of a Beaumont appraisal?
faqs.a: The Appraisal Review Board, once you file with Jefferson Central Appraisal District. The filing limit is whichever comes later, May 15 or 30 days after your notice was mailed.
